title: NanoDrop One spectrophotometer
manualMd: 1-2 μL micro-volume UV-Vis spec for nucleic acids and protein. Reports A260, A280, A260/A280, A260/A230. Ideal range: 2-3700 ng/μL dsDNA. Use the cuvette mode for samples below 2 ng/μL.
hazardsMd:
- The pedestal arm pinches; lower it gently.
- Many sample buffers contain phenol or guanidine — wear gloves.

operations.title: Daily startup
operations.bodyMd: Power on. Lift the arm; wipe both pedestals with a Kimwipe. Run a 'water blank' to verify the baseline reads 0.00 ± 0.02 absorbance.

operations.title: Measure dsDNA
operations.bodyMd:
1. Select Nucleic Acid → dsDNA.
2. Blank with the buffer your sample is in (NOT water if elution is in TE).
3. Pipette 1 μL of sample on the pedestal. Lower arm. Read.
4. Wipe both pedestals with a fresh Kimwipe between samples.

operations.title: Bad A260/A280
operations.bodyMd: Pure dsDNA reads ≈ 1.8. Below 1.7 = protein contamination. Above 2.0 = RNA or contamination from blank mismatch. Re-blank with the correct buffer and re-measure; if persistent, repurify.

operations.title: Sample beads up
operations.bodyMd: Pedestal needs cleaning. Wipe with 0.5 M HCl, then water, then a Kimwipe. The beading suggests residue or the pedestal is hydrophobic again.

operations.title: Post-use
operations.bodyMd: Wipe both pedestals dry. Lower the arm. Log out of your account.
